note: Donor-owned executable rubric for the deterministic fleet scan. ripgrep (PCRE) regexes, run over *.ts/*.tsx (excluding tests/node_modules). The dashboard moleculeAudit scanner reads this from the connected baseline; promotion-radar.json candidates reference a molecule signal id via `scanSignal`. Novel-pattern discovery is NOT here — that stays the periodic LLM audit.
adoptionQualityNote: Axis-C (adoption-quality) tripwires — see docs/ADOPTION-QUALITY.md. Every entry is gated by `coOccursWith` (a PCRE alternation of the archetype's shell import names) so it ONLY fires when the file actually adopts that archetype. A tripwire is a CANDIDATE, never a verdict — the per-page LLM acceptance-gate pass (the `## Acceptance gate` in docs/archetypes/<slug>.md) decides. tier: red = almost certainly a wrapper failure; yellow = likely, needs the gate to confirm. Regexes are deliberately loose/cheap; false positives are fine because the gate filters them.

adoptionQuality.shouldBe: primary records/breakdown are always-visible <DetailSection>s; tabs only for secondary surfaces

adoptionQuality.smell: action buttons in PageHeader's actions slot on a list page
adoptionQuality.shouldBe: all page-level actions belong in the toolbar (ListWithDetail Layer 4)

adoptionQuality.smell: a button row or page header rendered as a JSX sibling ABOVE the shell (the named wrapper tell in list-with-detail's acceptance gate) — indentation-matched, so best-effort: needs human triage, a legit banner above the shell reads the same
adoptionQuality.shouldBe: write actions in the shell's toolbar, header affordances in headerActions — nothing above the shell (ListWithDetail Layer 4)

adoptionQuality.smell: hand-rolled grid of <Card>s next to/instead of the shell
adoptionQuality.shouldBe: use <ListWithDetailShell presentation="card-grid"> — the conformant variant

adoptionQuality.smell: Save/Submit action wired into the form header
adoptionQuality.shouldBe: form actions live only in <FormPageFooter>

adoptionQuality.smell: hand-rolled max-w + padding wrapper around a form

adoptionQuality.smell: window.confirm as the J discard guard — crudStrings.confirmDiscard is a demo stand-in, and consumers ship it to production unchanged: a native dialog that breaks the app's visual language and blocks the JS thread, one contract-layer from the in-app <AlertDialog> the same dialogs use for delete (Layer 14)
adoptionQuality.shouldBe: a promise-based in-app <AlertDialog> confirm passed as useCrudDialogMode's onConfirmDiscard; route the close path through mode.requestDiscard() so both exit paths share it. The donor's own crudStrings.ts definition is the one expected residual hit — the gate clears it by confirming no consumer passes it
